title: Building Your First MCP Server
description: Create a small MCP server in C# that exposes tools and resources, and test it with an MCP client.

blocks.text: In this lesson, you build a minimal MCP server that wraps a simple C# service. The server exposes a tool for searching products and a resource for customer data. You test it locally using stdio.
Use an MCP inspector or client that supports stdio to verify tool discovery and invocation. Confirm that the client can see your tools, request execution, and receive structured results.

blocks.title: Full stdio MCP server setup
blocks.content: Complete Program.cs with DI registration, tool registration, and a sample tool class.

blocks.title: Keep the first server tiny
blocks.text: One tool and one resource are enough for the first version. Add complexity only after you have tested the full discovery and invocation loop.

blocks.title: Create Your First MCP Server
blocks.description: Build a working MCP server with one tool and one resource.
steps: Create a console app with the MCP SDK package.
Wrap an existing in-memory or database-backed service.
Expose one tool and one resource.
Run the server and inspect available primitives with an MCP client.
blocks.expectedOutcome: You should see your tool and resource from the client, and successfully invoke the tool with valid arguments.
